from fractions import Fraction

# Finite model of the claim under test:
# H: wearing less on cold, overcast days CAUSES arthritis.
# Option D: many people who wear more on such days also get arthritis,
# and most of them are middle-aged or elderly.
#
# Individuals are (wears_less, age_group, arthritis). Age is the only
# variable that drives arthritis in this alternative model, so any
# association with wears_less comes from confounding by age.

ages = ["young", "middle", "elderly"]
arthritis_rate = {"young": Fraction(1, 10), "middle": Fraction(3, 10), "elderly": Fraction(6, 10)}
N = 100  # people per (wears_less, age) cell

population = []
for wl in (True, False):
    for age in ages:
        # Assumed: wearing less is more common among young people.
        group_size = {"young": 60, "middle": 25, "elderly": 15} if wl else {"young": 15, "middle": 25, "elderly": 60}
        n = group_size[age]
        k = int(arthritis_rate[age] * n)  # exact count (all sizes chosen to divide cleanly)
        for i in range(n):
            population.append((wl, age, i < k))

def count(pred):
    return sum(1 for p in population if pred(p))

total = len(population)
wl_total = count(lambda p: p[0])
wm_total = count(lambda p: not p[0])
wl_arth = count(lambda p: p[0] and p[2])
wm_arth = count(lambda p: (not p[0]) and p[2])
wm_arth_old_mid = count(lambda p: (not p[0]) and p[2] and p[1] in ("middle", "elderly"))

print("total population:", total)
print("wear-less total:", wl_total, "arthritis:", wl_arth)
print("wear-more total:", wm_total, "arthritis:", wm_arth)
print("wear-more arthritis, middle/elderly:", wm_arth_old_mid)
print("arthritis rate wear-less:", Fraction(wl_arth, wl_total))
print("arthritis rate wear-more:", Fraction(wm_arth, wm_total))

# Under H, wear-more people should have essentially no arthritis.
# D's pattern requires wear-more arthritis cases to exist and to be mostly middle/elderly.
d_consistent = (wm_arth > 0) and (wm_arth_old_mid * 2 > wm_arth)

# Confounding check: within each age group, the clothing association disappears
# (arthritis depends only on age in this model).
within_age_ok = True
for age in ages:
    rates = []
    for wl in (True, False):
        cell = [p for p in population if p[0] == wl and p[1] == age]
        rates.append(Fraction(sum(1 for p in cell if p[2]), len(cell)))
    if rates[0] != rates[1]:
        within_age_ok = False
    print(f"age={age} rate wear-less={rates[0]} wear-more={rates[1]}")

# Option D, if true, is consistent with the age-confounding model and shows
# arthritis occurring without the claimed cause, so it undermines H.
if d_consistent and within_age_ok:
    print("Option D pattern is consistent with an age-based alternative explanation.")
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")

# Scope note: this is a constructed model, not evidence about real patients.
# It shows D's claim is coherent and undermines the causal reading. It does not
# prove D is the intended answer over other options (e.g., C also questions H,
# but from a single case, so it is weaker).
print("Sampling/model scope: constructed finite model; no real-world data verified.")
